exposure: cervical ripening balloon placement for 6 hours
cervical ripening balloon placement for 12 hours
outcome: cesarean delivery due to fetal distress
cesarean delivery due to other indications
cohort: The study included 171 patients with one prior low-segment cesarean delivery undergoing labor induction with a cervical ripening balloon.
finding: Removing the cervical ripening balloon after 6 hours, as opposed to 12 hours, does not negatively impact VBAC rates or other key maternal and neonatal outcomes in patients with a previous cesarean delivery.
mod_finding: The duration of cervical ripening balloon placement (6h vs 12h) did not significantly impact the rate of vaginal birth after cesarean (VBAC) or other modes of delivery.
